{"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"### 🚀 **Performance Optimization Plan (A3) – Resuming Task** **For:** Next LLM Agent (Continuing from Handoff Summary) --- ## ✅ **Objective** Deliver a **performance optimization plan** that ensures **P99 API response time ≤ 75ms** for all public `/profile` endpoints, while maintaining **SSE-KMS encryption compliance** and enabling **real-time observability** via distributed tracing. This builds directly on the prior work: - Security: SSE-KMS enforced by A2/A4. - SLA: P99 ≤ 75ms is non-negotiable. - Observability: X-Ray/OpenTelemetry required. We now focus on **latency mitigation**, **load testing**, and **guardrail design** — *without duplicating* encryption or policy work already underway. --- ## 🔧 **1. Performance Optimization Strategy (Core Pillars)** | Pillar | Strategy | Rationale | |-------|--------|---------| | **Caching Layer** | Implement **multi-tier caching**:
• **Edge Caching (CloudFront)**: Cache `/profile/{id}` at edge (TTL: 60s)
• **In-Memory Cache (Redis)**: Store hot profiles (TTL: 300s), with invalidation on update | Reduces DB load; serves 80%+ of reads from cache. Critical for low-latency. | | **Database Query Tuning** | Optimize profile query:
• Use **GSI (Global Secondary Index)** on `user_id` in DynamoDB
• Limit projection to only needed fields (`name`, `email`, `avatar_url`) | Avoids full table scans; reduces read capacity & latency. | | **Connection Pooling** | Enforce **connection pooling** in backend (e.g., HikariCP for JDBC, or async HTTP clients like OkHttp/HTTPX) | Prevents connection exhaustion under high RPS. | | **Asynchronous Processing** | Offload non-critical operations (e.g., analytics logging, audit trails) to async queues (SQS + Lambda) | Keeps request path synchronous and fast. | | **Edge Optimization** | Enable **CloudFront compression (gzip/brotli)** and **HTTP/2** | Reduces payload size and improves transfer speed. | --- ## 📊 **2. Load Testing Plan (Simulating 10K RPS)** ### 🎯 **Goal**: Validate P99 ≤ 75ms under sustained 10K RPS. #### ✅ **Test Setup** - **Tool**: AWS Step Functions + Lambda (for scalable test orchestration) or **AWS Proton + App Mesh** for real-world simulation. - **Load Generator**: Use **AWS Lambda-based stress test runners** (via `aws lambda invoke`) or **k6** (open-source) deployed across multiple AZs. - **Target Endpoint**: `/profile/{id}` (public, unauthenticated). - **Payload Sample** (from references): ```json { "id": "usr-12345", "name": "Alice Johnson", "email": "alice@example.com", "avatar_url": "https://cdn.example.com/avatars/12345.jpg" } ``` #### ⏱️ **Metrics to Track** | Metric | Target | Tool | |------|--------|------| | P99 Response Time | ≤ 75ms | CloudWatch + X-Ray | | Error Rate | < 0.1% | CloudWatch Alarms | | Throughput | ≥ 10,000 RPS | k6 / Lambda metrics | | Latency Distribution | 90% < 50ms, 99% < 75ms | X-Ray Service Map + Trace Sampling | #### 🔄 **Test Phases** 1. **Baseline Test (No Caching)**: Confirm current baseline latency. 2. **Phase 1 (Cache Enabled)**: Add CloudFront + Redis layer → measure improvement. 3. **Phase 2 (Optimized DB + Async)**: Apply GSI + async logging → validate further gains. 4. **Phase 3 (Stress Test)**: Ramp to 10K RPS over 10 minutes → monitor P99. > ✅ **Success Criteria**: P99 ≤ 75ms **across all phases**. --- ## 🛡️ **3. Performance Guardrails (Proactive Mitigation)** | Guardrail | Implementation | Purpose | |---------|----------------|--------| | **Rate Limiting** | Use **API Gateway Throttling** (per-user/IP): 100 req/sec burst, 10 req/sec steady | Prevents abuse & protects backend. | | **Timeouts** | Set **client-side timeout = 50ms**, **server-side = 100ms** | Ensures fast failure, avoids cascading delays. | | **Circuit Breaker** | Integrate **Hystrix** or **Resilience4j** on DB/cache calls | Stops failing requests during outages. | | **Auto-Scaling** | Configure **DynamoDB autoscaling** + **Lambda concurrency limits** | Maintains performance under load spikes. | | **Monitoring Alerts** | Create CloudWatch alarms:
• P99 > 75ms → trigger SNS alert
• Error rate > 0.1% → notify A3/A2 | Enables rapid incident response. | --- ## 📌 **4. Integration with Observability Stack** ### ✅ **Distributed Tracing (X-Ray + OpenTelemetry)** - Instrument all services with **OpenTelemetry SDK** (auto-instrumentation via agent). - Enable **X-Ray sampling (100%)** for `/profile` endpoint. - Trace spans must include: - `db.query.duration` - `cache.hit` - `http.request.size` - `lambda.invocation.duration` > 🔍 **Use Case**: If P99 exceeds 75ms, use X-Ray trace to identify bottleneck (e.g., slow DB call vs. cache miss). ### 📈 **Dashboarding** - Build **CloudWatch Dashboard** with: - Real-time P99 latency graph - Cache hit ratio - Error rate per region - Request count (RPS) --- ## 📎 **Critical References Used** - [AWS S3 Encryption Enforcement Policy](#) (already provided) - [OpenTelemetry Instrumentation Guide (AWS)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-RUM-configure-opentelemetry.html) - [X-Ray Best Practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-bestpractices.html) - [k6 Load Testing Example](https://k6.io/docs/) - [DynamoDB GSI Optimization Tips](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/best-practices.html#query-patterns) --- ## ✅ **Deliverables for Handoff to A2 & A4** 1. **Performance Optimization Plan Document** (this summary). 2. **Load Test Script & Results Report** (after execution). 3. **Guardrail Configuration Snippets** (API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB). 4. **Observability Dashboard Link** (CloudWatch URL). 5. **Recommendations for A2/A4**: - A2: Ensure IAM roles allow access to KMS key used in SSE-KMS. - A4: Confirm cache keys are invalidated on profile updates (via event-driven triggers). --- > ✅ **Handoff Ready** – This plan is **ready for implementation** by A3 (Performance Specialist). > Next step: Execute load tests, collect data, and validate P99 ≤ 75ms. > Once validated, share results with A2 for final compliance sign-off. --- 📌 **Note**: No duplication of encryption logic or bucket policy work — those are already locked in by A2/A4. Focus remains strictly on **performance, observability, and guardrails**.","role":"assistant"}}],"created":1786859480,"id":"chatcmpl-c20a33cd-4747-97bd-b4f4-676b9210d440","model":"qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-instruct-2507","object":"chat.completion","usage":{"completion_tokens":1725,"prompt_tokens":929,"total_tokens":2654}}
